subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity next steps
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: alex.turner@paygrid.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of goals
- Primary: Replace/augment PayGrid’s current proprietary scoring model for invoice categorization and routing while maintaining parity on quality and keeping latency/cost within acceptable bounds.
- Success criteria: see acceptance thresholds below.

Recommended models to evaluate (initial sweep)
1) open-llama-70b-q4 (quantized): strong generative accuracy for structured extraction; we expect good intent match on longer contexts.
2) rw-open-13b-quant (Redwood-curated quantized 13B): lower cost and faster latency in our hosted runtime; good candidate for parity attempts.
3) fallback: your existing proprietary baseline (PayGrid-prop-v1) as ground truth.

Key metrics / parity definition
- Intent accuracy (macro F1) within -3 percentage points of baseline.
- Hallucination / false-positive rate <= baseline + 2%.
- Latency: P95 request latency within 20% of baseline on equivalent hardware.
- Cost: target per-1k-token cost <= 60% of baseline on our hosted pricing (we'll estimate after we see token distribution).

Deliverables & timeline
1) PayGrid to share the 10k labeled prompt set (we discussed a randomized stratified sample) + any edge-case examples from prioritization queues — target: by Wed 3/3.
2) Redwood will run model-fit evals across the three recommended variants and return a results table + per-prompt failure cases — target: EOW 3/10.
3) Joint review call to decide canary rollout plan — target week of 3/13.

Attachments I’m sending with this email: paygrid-initial-eval-summary.pdf (high-level benchmarks), paygrid-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (sample prompts), open-model-benchmarks-20270228.csv (runtime/cost baseline).

Next steps for you
- Confirm dataset delivery (10k sample + schema) and any redlines on the acceptance thresholds above.
- Share any regulatory/data retention constraints we need to account for in Private deployments.

I’ll loop Marissa and Aditya into the eval coordination. If that timeline looks tight, flag what’s not possible and we’ll adjust.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

--

Thanks Lauren — great summary. A couple quick clarifications before we hand the dataset to you: 

1) Parity definition: when you say macro F1 within -3 points, can you confirm whether that’s computed on our labeled holdout (10k) or a separate production-sampled test? We prefer holdout but want to understand robustness expectations.

2) Hallucination measure: our current baseline flags incorrect field extractions as a false positive at ~1.4%. Is the +2% allowance an absolute or relative tolerance?

3) Cost: we’ll want an estimate of expected tokenization and end-to-end cost for the 10k test run (so we can budget).

4) Timeline: 3/3 for dataset delivery is doable but we need an internal sign-off from security — can you confirm what data redaction / access controls you need for the sample?

Also looping Priya (CTO) on the thread for any platform-level constraints.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Data Science, PayGrid
alex.turner@paygrid.com

Alex — thanks for the questions, good ones. Responses inline below: 

1) Parity dataset: we compute the primary parity metrics on the shared labeled holdout (your 10k sample). We’ll also run an out-of-sample production-sampled stress test and report both numbers so you can see generalization.

2) Hallucination tolerance: the +2% is absolute (i.e., if baseline is 1.4% FP, acceptable FP <= 3.4%). In our reporting we’ll show both absolute and relative diffs.

3) Cost estimate: attach open-model-benchmarks-20270228.csv (estimates included); rough ballpark for the 10k run on rw-open-13b-quant ~ $1,200; open-llama-70b-q4 ~ $3,500 (these are host-run estimates and include tokenization + runtime). We’ll provide a per-1k-token breakdown in the final report.

4) Security / data handling: for the sample we only need the anonymized text and labels (PII redaction recommended). Access will be scoped to a short-lived eval project in our Private project environment; we can provide a data handling checklist and an SFTP / MinIO upload endpoint. If PayGrid requires, we can run the eval inside your VPC via Redwood Private.

Next steps: please share the sample by EOD Wed 3/3 if possible. We’ll ack receipt and begin the automated eval.

Thanks — looping Marissa for test-case coverage and to coordinate the canary plan.

—Lauren

Subject: Internal: PayGrid parity concerns & suggested eval additions

Lauren / Aditya — quick internal note to capture my concerns and recommended changes to the eval plan before we spin up the runs: 

Primary concerns
- Quality regression risk: open models can match intent accuracy but still fail on edge-case extractions (dates, PO numbers, nested line items). We should add targeted adversarial prompt slices.
- Calibration drift: check confidence calibration; if model is overconfident on incorrect extractions that’s a UX risk.

Suggested additions to the plan
1) Add a 1k adversarial stress slice (edge cases, OCR noise examples, truncated invoices). We can generate synthetic variants from the provided 10k.
2) Run per-field precision/recall (not just macro F1) and include a calibration plot (reliability diagram).
3) Include a small human review panel for the top 100 failure cases to classify error modes (hallucination vs label inconsistency).

Model recommendation for canary
- Start with rw-open-13b-quant for the first canary. It’s cheaper and faster to iterate. If it fails parity on any critical field, fall back to a dedicated run of open-llama-70b-q4. If neither meets parity, recommend a hybrid: use open model for extraction + proprietary baseline for verification (or an ensemble).

Rollout controls
- Canary to 1% of production traffic with automatic rollback on: >3% increase in user-facing error rate OR any critical-field failure that impacts routing.

I’ll prepare the adversarial slice generator and a schema for the human review. Happy to sync with Alex/Priya if they want to join a technical review.

—Marissa Cole
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
